blocks.text: North Coquitlam Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: North Coquitlam is the board name for Coquitlam's City Centre tower district, so expect the same streets to be called City Centre or Town Centre in City documents: the condo and townhouse stock clusters on Pinetree Way, Glen Drive, Atlantic Avenue and Pinewood Avenue, around Coquitlam City Hall at 3000 Guildford Way.

Town Centre Park at 1299 Pinetree Way is the district's north anchor, a 100-acre park holding Lafarge Lake, Percy Perry Stadium and the City Centre Aquatic Complex area, with Pinetree Secondary School beside it.

The district's project architect for its newest tower site describes 1175 Pinetree Way as a block away from Coquitlam City Hall and Coquitlam Town Centre Park, which is the working centre of this page's area.
Coquitlam Public Library's City Centre Branch at 1169 Pinetree Way sits inside the cluster, on the same street as the towers and the park.

blocks.text: North Coquitlam Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: MThree at 1188 Pinetree Way is the tower whose facts the developer itself publishes: Cressey's own project page confirms a 48-storey tower with 319 homes, completed in 2016, with The Summit Club, 9,000 square feet of amenities, at the top of the building.

The City Centre Area Plan Schedule A legend is the plan source for the district's form mix: it designates apartment and townhousing areas closer to City Centre, alongside one-family designations farther out, which is why this page's stock is towers and podium townhomes rather than detached houses.

The next stock arriving is mixed tenure, not all strata: Onni Group's own leasing material for Pine & Glen at 3022 Glen Drive states over 900 residential units with 35,000 square feet of office space and 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, so a share of the district's new homes will be rental-only and never appear as strata resales.

blocks.text: North Coquitlam Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Town Centre Park is undergoing upgrades guided by the Town Centre Park Master Plan, approved in 2018 to guide improvements for 15 to 20 years, and the City warns some trails close while work is under way — a live construction factor for park-facing units.

The park's Community Plaza, on the eastern shore of Lafarge Lake, seats up to 1,300 people and is one of the region's outdoor performance and event venues, so event noise is a Lafarge Lake-facing unit check, not a district-wide one.
Percy Perry Stadium's track and the park's five lit synthetic turf fields and eight lit tennis courts put evening sports lighting on the park's edge, closest to the Pinetree Way towers.
The City Centre Branch library at 1169 Pinetree Way and the City archives at 1171 Pinetree Way share the tower district's main street.

blocks.text: North Coquitlam Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Pine & Glen, 1175 Pinetree Way at Glen Drive (commercial leasing address 3022 Glen Drive), Onni Group, mixed-use towers: over 900 residential units, 35,000 square feet of office and 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail in the developer's own brochure, with north and west retail units listed as available Q1 2027 and office floors available Q1 2027 — status: under construction with commercial pre-leasing open (as of November 3, 2026).

Town Centre Park upgrades, 1299 Pinetree Way, City of Coquitlam: park improvements under the 2018 Town Centre Park Master Plan, including a Percy Perry Stadium track closure notice and tennis court maintenance beginning May 25, 2026 — status: phased upgrades under way (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: North Coquitlam Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: The Millennium Line Evergreen Extension is this district's rapid transit: the City places the Lafarge Lake–Douglas terminus in Town Centre Park's southwest corner, and Coquitlam Central Station, with West Coast Express service, sits at the district's south end.
Route 186, Coquitlam Central Station to Hampton Park, runs Pinetree Way and David Avenue at the district's north side via Pipeline Road and Robson Drive.

blocks.text: North Coquitlam home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

195 condos sold in North Coquitlam with a median price of $600,000 (the middle half sold between $510,000 and $669,000), taking a median of 23 days to sell at 97.3% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $684 per square foot, a median year built of 2009 and a median strata fee of $460 a month. 3 townhomes sold in North Coquitlam, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in North Coquitlam?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 136 condos and townhomes listed in North Coquitlam. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is North Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in North Coquitlam had a sales ratio of 18%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in North Coquitlam from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 111 condos and townhomes sold in North Coquitlam over those 5 months, out of 596 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: Is North Coquitlam the same place as Coquitlam City Centre?
faq.a: Yes, for this housing stock. North Coquitlam is the board sub-area name, while the City calls the same Pinetree Way, Glen Drive and Guildford Way district City Centre or Town Centre in its plans and facility pages. A buyer searching only one name misses listings filed under the other, so check both labels for the tower cluster around Town Centre Park and City Hall.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve a Pinetree Way condo?
faq.a: Two stations bracket the cluster. The City places the Lafarge Lake–Douglas Station terminus of the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension in the southwest corner of Town Centre Park, and Onni's own material for Pine & Glen describes the site as within walking distance of both Coquitlam Central Station and the Lafarge Lake/Douglas Station. Lincoln Station sits between them on the same line.

faq.q: Which schools are physically inside this condo district?
faq.a: School District No. 43 (Coquitlam), called SD43, lists Pinetree Secondary at 3000 Pinewood Avenue for Grades 9 to 12, Pinetree Way Elementary at 1420 Pinetree Way for kindergarten to Grade 5, and Glen Elementary at 3064 Glen Drive, all inside the tower district's streets.

faq.q: What will Pine & Glen change for existing condo owners here?
faq.a: Onni Group's own leasing brochure describes Pine & Glen on Glen Drive as a mixed-use development in the heart of Coquitlam with over 900 residential units, 35,000 square feet of office space and 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, with retail units available in the first quarter of 2027. That is new supply, new retail and new office workers arriving beside the existing Glen Drive towers.

faq.q: What did condos in North Coquitlam sell for?
faq.a: 195 condos sold in North Coquitlam between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $600,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in North Coquitlam?
faq.a: The median was 23 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.3% of the last list price (4% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
